- DARZALEX royalty stream: $14.0 billion, 53% of the total. This is the largest single piece and the one most people ignore. Daratumumab did $4,207 million of net sales in the second quarter of 2026, annualising to about $16.8 billion; at roughly a 19% effective royalty rate that is about $3.2 billion a year of essentially costless income to Genmab. We model it growing to about $3.6 billion by 2029, then declining roughly 30% a year as exclusivity lapses, discounted at 9%. That gives just under $14 billion. It is a wasting asset with a date on it, not a perpetuity, and valuing it as a perpetuity is the most common error made with this company.
- Other royalties (Kesimpta, Tecvayli, Talvey, Rybrevant): $2.9 billion, 11%. Roughly $450 million a year, growing, longer-dated than daratumumab, at about six and a half times.
- EPKINLY and TIVDAK, the medicines Genmab sells itself: $4.0 billion, 15%. Proprietary sales were $632 million in 2025 and $176 million in the first quarter of 2026, growing 43%. We deliberately do not capitalise gross product sales, because Genmab shares the economics roughly fifty-fifty with AbbVie on EPKINLY in its main territories and with Pfizer on TIVDAK. Genmab's claim on the cash is about half of what the headline sales figure suggests.
- Rina-S: $3.3 billion, 13%. Above the roughly $1.8 billion Genmab paid for ProfoundBio in 2024, reflecting genuine de-risking since: a breakthrough designation, three Phase 3 trials running, and the ovarian Phase 3 fully enrolled ahead of plan. Below the company's $2 billion-plus peak guidance capitalised in full, because none of it is approved.
- Petosemtamab: $5.5 billion, 21%. Genmab paid roughly $8 billion for Merus. We carry it below cost, and deliberately, because the asset has not been de-risked since the purchase; the two Phase 3 readouts that would justify the price are still ahead. If they land, this part alone is worth roughly 370 kroner per share more.
- Remaining pipeline and platform: $0.5 billion, 2%.
- Less net debt at 30 June 2026: minus $3.8 billion, minus 402 kroner per share. This is a liability and we subtract it. It is $5.13 billion of borrowings plus $138 million of capitalised leases, less $1.50 billion of cash. Nine months earlier this line was a positive $1.6 billion of net cash. Filings often quote about $3.63 billion, excluding leases; we use the inclusive figure.
Cross-check: our 2,800 sits above the analyst consensus target of about $38.25 per depositary receipt, roughly 2,490 kroner, and above the median of $39, roughly 2,540. The gap is almost entirely petosemtamab, which we carry at $5.5 billion and which the street has not yet put a number on at all, because the company itself refuses to guide one.
risk_reward: Poor on the base case, good only on the favourable one, and that is the whole argument. From 2,261 kroner, our adverse case is 1,450 and our base case is 2,800, so you are risking roughly 811 kroner to make roughly 539. The favourable case at 4,350 is worth about 2,089, so the shape only becomes attractive if you underwrite the petosemtamab and Rina-S readouts landing, which is exactly what has not been proven yet. Put differently: the discount to our base case is about 19%, which falls short of the 20% minimum entry discount this book requires even in the friendliest market conditions. There is no structural floor beneath the shares. This is a net borrower with $3.77 billion of debt, no dividend, no active buyback, and $8.87 billion of intangibles against $5.96 billion of equity. The nearest technical reference points are the 200-day average around 1,888 and the 52-week low of 1,512, and neither of those is a floor in any structural sense.
peer_comps_note:
We were given argenx, Regeneron, BioNTech and Immunocore as comparable antibody businesses, with a house verdict of cheap versus peers. We do not adopt that verdict, and we want to be explicit about why, because the reasoning behind it is wrong in a specific and correctable way. The peer note attributes the minus 82% revenue print to a base-effect artifact from a large prior-year Darzalex-related milestone payment. That is not what happened. Genmab changed its reporting currency from Danish kroner to US dollars with the 2025 accounts: 21.53 billion kroner in 2024 became $3.86 billion in 2025, and the ratio of those two numbers is exactly the minus 82.1% printed. It is a units error in our screen, not a milestone. The conclusion happens to be directionally right for the wrong reason, which is the most dangerous kind of right.

The file carries no current peer multiple and no anchor multiple, so we will not quote one from memory; peer multiples de-rate and a stale anchor would inflate the apparent discount. We use the peer set structurally instead. Regeneron is the instructive one, and it is a warning rather than a comfort: a scaled, genuinely innovative antibody company whose rating compressed hard once the market decided that erosion of its anchor product was real, in spite of a broad and funded pipeline. That is precisely Genmab's situation around the end of this decade, with daratumumab in the anchor role. argenx runs the opposite way, a single-product growth story rated on what is still ahead of it; Genmab is a hybrid, with a wasting royalty paying for a pipeline that has not yet arrived. BioNTech and Immunocore are platform companies without a comparable installed royalty base, so the read-across is weak.

On the numbers that do travel: the 18.2 times free cash flow in our scan ignores $3.77 billion of net debt. Measured properly on enterprise value against $870 million of trailing free cash flow, the multiple is about 29 times. On consensus earnings the shares trade at roughly 29 times 2026 and 20 times 2027. The discounted-cash-flow fair value of 8,088 kroner in our scan is computed off the broken revenue series and should be discarded outright. One caution that applies to the whole group rather than to Genmab alone: government price negotiation on high-spend medicines is a shared factor across every large biopharma name here. Any discount Genmab carries on that account is sector-wide and not a name-specific edge, and we do not credit it as one.

# Genmab A/S (Copenhagen listing) — Forensic Dossier
*Prepared 22 September 2026. Price used throughout: 2,261 Danish kroner per Copenhagen share, the live quote on 22 September 2026. The company also trades in New York as a depositary receipt at $34.69, with ten receipts to one Copenhagen share.*

---

## 1. Narrative arc

Across the eight quarters in front of us — from the first quarter of 2025 through the first quarter of 2026 — Genmab tells one story, and it tells it consistently. The company is converting itself from a royalty collector into a drug company that owns and sells its own medicines.

At the start of the window (May 2025) the language is about becoming "a fully integrated biotech independently developing and commercializing wholly owned antibody differentiated therapies." Three assets carry the weight: epcoritamab, sold as EPKINLY, a lymphoma antibody partnered with AbbVie; Rina-S, an antibody-drug conjugate for ovarian and endometrial cancer acquired with ProfoundBio; and acasunlimab, an immune-activating antibody.

Three things changed over the eight quarters, and each one matters more than the steady commercial progress that dominates the prepared remarks.

**First, the balance sheet flipped.** In the first three calls, cash is a headline and a boast: "over $3 billion in cash" (first quarter 2025), "around $3 billion" (first half 2025), "around $3.4 billion" (first nine months of 2025), each time followed by the phrase "flexibility for continued growth and expansion." Then in November 2025 the company announced the proposed acquisition of Merus, funded with a $5.5 billion debt offering. By 30 June 2026 the balance sheet shows $1.50 billion of cash against $5.27 billion of total borrowings — net debt of $3.77 billion. Nine months earlier, on 30 September 2025, the same company had $3.41 billion of cash and investments against $142 million of lease obligations: net *cash* of $1.62 billion. That is a $5.4 billion swing in three quarters, and it is the single largest fact in this file.

**Second, one of the three legs was replaced by a fourth, larger, more expensive one.** Acasunlimab quietly receded — it goes from a named growth driver in May 2025 to a melanoma trial mention in August 2025 to essentially absent by February 2026. GEN1042, the antibody partnered with BioNTech in head and neck cancer, was explicitly killed in November 2025: "the current data in frontline head and neck cancer for GEN1042 did not meet our high bar for continued development." In its place came petosemtamab, acquired with Merus and now described as the third multibillion-dollar asset. The company traded a home-grown head-and-neck programme it could not make work for a purchased head-and-neck programme, and paid roughly $8 billion for the privilege.

**Third, the emphasis shifted from data generation to data resolution.** Early calls are about starting trials, adding cohorts, accelerating enrolment. By February 2026 the framing is: "we expect up to 6 potentially registrational data readouts" in 2026. The company has stopped promising to build and started promising to prove.

---

## 2. Claims versus financials (forensic)

**The most important finding in this section is that our own screener is wrong, not management.**

| Management claim | What our data says | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Our total revenue grew by 19%" (2025) | Screener reads revenue down 82% year over year, with a three-year decline of 36% a year | **Management is right; the screener is broken.** Genmab changed its reporting currency from Danish kroner to US dollars with the 2025 accounts. Revenue of 21.53 billion kroner in 2024 became $3.86 billion in 2025. Divide the second by the first and you get exactly the −82.1% the screen prints. The screen compared kroner to dollars. Independent confirmation: trailing-twelve-month revenue to 30 June 2026 is $4.13 billion, and first-half 2026 revenue grew 25%. Nothing collapsed. |
| Revenue accelerating: +19% (Q1 2025), +19% (H1 2025), +21% (9M 2025), +19% (FY 2025), +25% (Q1 2026) | Trailing revenue $4.13 billion, up from $3.86 billion for the 2025 full year; first-half 2026 up 25% and the full-year outlook raised on 6 August 2026 | **Corroborated, and improving.** Growth is genuinely accelerating, not decelerating. |
| "Combined EPKINLY and Tivdak sales up 56%" (Q1 2025), "up 54%" (9M 2025), "43% growth" (Q1 2026) | Proprietary sales of $632 million in 2025, up 54%; $176 million in the first quarter of 2026 | **Corroborated.** Note the deceleration from 54-56% to 43% — still fast, but the law of larger numbers is arriving. |
| "We have grown operating profit by 62%" (Q1 2025), "by 56%" (H1 2025), "by 52%" (9M 2025) | Not independently checkable from our data for those quarters, but the direction is consistent with trailing operating profit of $1.33 billion on $4.13 billion of revenue — a 32% operating margin | **Plausible, but watch what happened next.** |
| "We have also grown operating profit even while making these strategic investments" (FY 2025); "we grew operating profits" (Q1 2026) | Same measure, no number attached | 🔴 **The specificity vanished exactly when the leverage arrived.** For three consecutive calls the operating-profit growth rate was quantified to the percentage point. From the full-year 2025 call onward it is an unquantified assertion. That is the clearest tone change in the file, and it coincides with the Merus debt. |
| "$5.5 billion with roughly $2.5 billion of it being fixed... net, $4.1 billion is now fixed... weighted average effective interest rate of the debt is around 6.6%" (Anthony Pagano, FY 2025 call) | Total debt of $5.27 billion at 30 June 2026; trailing interest expense $269 million | 🟢 **Verifiable and verified.** This is high-quality disclosure — specific, checkable, and it checks. Note that $269 million on $5.27 billion is an effective 5.1% so far, because the debt was outstanding for only part of the trailing period. At the stated 6.6%, the full-year run-rate is roughly $350 million. Roughly $80 to $100 million of additional interest expense has still to land in the reported numbers. |
| "We've committed and remain committed to getting below 3x gross leverage by the end of 2027" | Gross debt of $5.27 billion against consensus 2026 earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation of about $1.25 billion is 4.2 times | 🔴 **A demanding promise.** On the consensus 2027 figure of about $1.55 billion, getting below three times requires gross debt under roughly $4.65 billion — about $600 million of repayment out of roughly $900 million to $1 billion of annual free cash flow, while funding five or more Phase 3 programmes. This is the constraint that keeps buybacks off the table. |
| "Rina-S... peak sales in ovarian and endometrial cancers exceeding $2 billion"; petosemtamab "multibillion dollar" | Nothing to test against — these are pre-approval assets | **Unfalsifiable today.** Note the asymmetry in the disclosure: the company will put a number on Rina-S ($2 billion plus) and on EPKINLY ($3 billion plus) but pointedly refuses to put one on petosemtamab, the asset it paid roughly $8 billion for. |
| Valuation models in our own scan: discounted-cash-flow fair value of 8,088 kroner; margin of safety of 11%; free cash flow multiple of 18.2 times | Trailing free cash flow $870 million; market value 138.8 billion kroner; net debt $3.77 billion | 🔴 **Discard the model outputs.** The discounted-cash-flow figure is built on the same broken revenue series and should be ignored entirely. The 18.2 times free cash flow multiple ignores $3.77 billion of net debt; on enterprise value — market value plus net debt — the multiple is about 29 times. The "deep value" label attached to this name is an artifact end to end. |

The balance sheet carries one more number that deserves to be read out loud: **$8.87 billion of intangible assets against $5.96 billion of total shareholders' equity.** Those intangibles are, overwhelmingly, petosemtamab and Rina-S. The accounting value of two drugs that have never been approved exceeds the entire book value of the company.

---

## 3. Tone and confidence trajectory

**Rating: Rising in substance, but shifting from offensive to defensive in posture.**

- **Q1 2025 (May):** Maximum offence. "Over $3 billion in cash, reinforcing the strength of our financial foundation. And this strength gives us the flexibility for continued growth and expansion." A share buyback of up to 2.2 million shares was initiated in March.
- **H1 2025 (August):** Still offensive, and now with the strongest clinical result in the file — the EPCORE FL-1 trial hit both of its primary goals, cutting the risk of disease progression or death by 79%. Management calls the results "unprecedented," twice. The buyback completed in June.
- **9M 2025 (November):** The pivot. Cash rises to $3.4 billion, and in the same breath the company announces it is spending far more than that on Merus, plus a $5.5 billion debt raise. The word "disciplined" appears repeatedly — "disciplined capital allocation," "disciplined investment into the highest potential programs" — which is what companies say when they are about to do something large.
- **FY 2025 (February 2026):** Confidence in the science is at its peak ("2026 will be a defining year"), but the financial language turns to leverage management. The operating-profit growth number disappears. And the company has to disclose its first real Phase 3 disappointment.
- **Q1 2026 (May):** Genuinely strong. Revenue up 25%, the ovarian cancer Phase 3 fully enrolled ahead of plan, the hospitalisation requirement removed from the EPKINLY label. But the prepared remarks now end with a list of things that will be proven later rather than things proven already.

The direction of travel is clear: the company is more confident about its drugs and more careful about its money than it was eighteen months ago.

---

## 4. Guidance credibility

**Reliability: High.** This is the strongest part of the file, and it argues against treating management's promises as cheap.

Things they said they would do, and did:
- Said in February 2025 they would start a Phase 3 in endometrial cancer "before the end of the year" — started, confirmed November 2025.
- Said they would present ovarian cancer follow-up data "early in the first half of 2025" — presented at the March 2025 oncology meeting, as promised.
- Said in May 2025 a decision on GEN1042 would come "in the second half of this year" — the programme was killed in November 2025. Killing your own asset on schedule is a form of guidance delivery that deserves credit.
- Guided to three Rina-S Phase 3 trials by end-2025 — delivered.
- The follicular lymphoma application was accepted for priority review with a target decision date of 30 November 2025 — approved, confirmed on the February 2026 call.
- Enrolment repeatedly ran *ahead* of plan. The follicular and frontline lymphoma trials "accrued significantly faster than initially projected" (May 2025); the ovarian Phase 3 "completed enrollment," pulling its data into 2026 (May 2026). Timelines moving earlier is rarer and more informative than timelines moving later.

This corroborates the 71% earnings-beat rate (five of the last seven quarters) in the financials. There is no sandbagging pattern visible — if anything the company under-promises on timing and over-delivers, which is the benign version.

**The one genuine miss, and how it was handled.** In January 2026 the EPCORE DLBCL-1 trial of EPKINLY on its own in relapsed lymphoma improved progression-free survival but, in management's words on the February 2026 call, "overall survival did not reach statistical significance." The very next sentence reached for reasons: "the potential impact of a variety of factors, including COVID-19 and the increasing availability of novel anti-lymphoma therapies." That is a textbook post-hoc explanation. The company then had to issue a formal clarification on the trial's primary endpoints on 23 July 2026 — seven months after the result. A result that needs clarifying two quarters later was not cleanly disclosed the first time. This is the single most important credibility mark against management in the file.

---

## 5. Analyst pressure points

Analysts pushed, repeatedly, on four things. Management deflected all four.

1. **What hazard ratio does the frontline lymphoma trial need?** Asked by Wolfe Research (Q1 2026) and by William Blair before it. Answer both times: "it doesn't make much sense to speculate." Fair as far as it goes — but it means the market has no management-anchored bar, so any result will be argued about rather than scored.
2. **Which of the six readouts comes first?** Asked by BNP Paribas and by others. Answer (Q1 2026): "I will not comment on which one first or second or together all these permutations that may exist." The company guides a half-year window and refuses to narrow it.
3. **What is petosemtamab actually worth in peak sales?** Handelsbanken asked directly (February 2026) what additional information is needed to replace "multibillion" with a number. Anthony Pagano: "I'm not going to front run this." For the company's largest-ever capital commitment, that is a conspicuous gap.
4. **Rina-S beyond ovarian and endometrial cancer.** Truist asked in May 2025 about the lung and other tumour cohorts. The answer contained a promise — "I promise you that very soon, we can also share in the public domain" — and a year later the public disclosure amounts to a lung trial and a gastrointestinal basket trial, with no data. The promise was warmer than the delivery.

**What analysts are not pressing on, and should be:** nobody in these transcripts asks what happens to the royalty stream when daratumumab — sold as DARZALEX by Johnson & Johnson, and the source of roughly seventy per cent of Genmab's revenue — loses exclusivity. Not one question. The entire analyst conversation is about the new drugs; the old one that pays for everything is treated as furniture.

---

## 6. Red flags and green flags

🔴 **Red flags**
- Net cash of $1.62 billion on 30 September 2025 became net debt of $3.77 billion on 30 June 2026. A $5.4 billion swing in three quarters, and the calls narrate the acquisition far more than they narrate the leverage.
- Quantified operating-profit growth (62%, 56%, 52%) stopped being quantified from the full-year 2025 call onward, exactly when the interest expense arrived.
- $8.87 billion of intangible assets against $5.96 billion of equity. Two unapproved drugs are carried at more than the whole book value of the company. A failed Phase 3 on petosemtamab is an impairment event, not just a pipeline disappointment.
- The lymphoma monotherapy trial missed on survival (January 2026), was explained away with COVID-19 and competing therapies, and needed a formal clarification seven months later (23 July 2026).
- Management's own bridge for petosemtamab — "Phase IIIs have in the past on EPKINLY tended to mimic close Phase II data" — is precisely the assumption the lymphoma monotherapy trial punctured. Petosemtamab's headline 63% response rate in first-line head and neck cancer is a single-arm Phase 2 number.
- The buyback completed in June 2025 has no successor. With a sub-three-times leverage promise due by the end of 2027, there will not be one soon.
- Insider buying ratio is zero across the scan window.

🟢 **Green flags**
- The delivery record is genuinely strong: trials started on time, enrolment ahead of plan, the regulatory decision date met, the follicular lymphoma Phase 3 hitting both goals with a 79% reduction in progression or death risk.
- Willingness to kill its own programme (GEN1042, November 2025) on the schedule it announced.
- Debt disclosure is unusually specific and checks against the balance sheet: $5.5 billion raised, $4.1 billion effectively fixed, 6.6% weighted average effective rate.
- Commercial execution is real and independent of the partner: first wholly owned launches in Japan and Europe, operations opened in Germany, the United Kingdom and France, and the hospitalisation requirement removed from the US lymphoma label in March 2026 — a label change that directly widens community use.
- Revenue growth is accelerating (19% to 25%) while the proprietary medicines grow 43% to 54%.

---

## 7. Hidden signals

- **The vocabulary of money changed.** "Flexibility for continued growth and expansion" (three consecutive calls) gave way to "below 3x gross leverage by the end of 2027." Same company, opposite posture.
- **"Very happy owners."** Anthony Pagano uses this phrase twice in one February 2026 answer, about petosemtamab and about Rina-S. Executives who are comfortable with a purchase describe its economics; executives reassuring themselves describe their happiness.
- **A promise with no number attached.** The company will guide peak sales for the two assets it built (EPKINLY above $3 billion, Rina-S above $2 billion) and will not guide the one it bought. The asymmetry runs the wrong way from a confidence standpoint.
- **The cash headline disappeared.** Cash was the first or second item in the prepared remarks for three straight calls, then stopped being mentioned as a highlight once it was spent.
- **Small, continuous share issuance.** Employee warrant exercises converted 185 shares on 16 June 2026, 24,592 on 11 August 2026 and 28,011 on 8 September 2026. Immaterial individually — roughly a tenth of a per cent a year — but it is standing, price-insensitive supply.
- **A holder stopping one basis point short of disclosure.** Orbis Investment Management reported 4.99% of the share capital on 15 June 2026. Five per cent is the Danish disclosure threshold. That is a deliberate stop.

---

## 8. Capital-allocation verdict (for the director)

**Classification: STRENGTHENING.** Revenue growth is accelerating, the proprietary medicines are growing 43% or better, the clinical delivery record is strong, and the full-year outlook was raised on 6 August 2026. This is not a company in trouble, and the "deep value" label our screen attached to it is an artifact of a currency change, not a judgement about the business.

**The single most important thing to weigh before sizing:** Genmab financed its entire future with borrowed money against two drugs that have not yet been approved, and the evidence that will tell you whether that was a good idea arrives in the next four months. Roughly seventy per cent of today's revenue is a royalty on someone else's product, daratumumab, whose exclusivity ends around the end of this decade. The $8 billion Merus purchase and the $5.5 billion of debt that paid for it are a bet that petosemtamab and Rina-S replace that royalty. Up to six potentially registrational readouts land between now and mid-2027, and the largest of them — the first-line head and neck cancer Phase 3 for petosemtamab — is the one that underwrites $8.87 billion of balance-sheet intangibles sitting on $5.96 billion of equity. You can watch that resolve for free. The stock is currently 1.2% below its 52-week high and 20% above its 200-day average, so you are not being paid to pre-position.

**Economic moat: NARROW, and stable rather than eroding.** The moat type is intangible — patented antibody engineering platforms and the regulatory exclusivity they earn. The evidence supports "narrow" rather than "wide": returns on invested capital of 12.6% are respectable but not fortress-grade, and they are mathematically falling, because the Merus acquisition roughly doubled invested capital while operating profit did not double. Gross margin of 91.7% is flagged as contracting, which is what happens when high-margin royalty revenue is diluted by lower-margin product sales the company manufactures and sells itself. Crucially, the moat has a *date* on it rather than a slope: the daratumumab royalty is a wasting asset with a scheduled end, not a franchise being competed away. I call the trend stable rather than eroding because the replacement is visibly being built and is so far delivering — the follicular lymphoma Phase 3 hit, the second-line lymphoma combination Phase 3 hit on 29 June 2026, European approval followed on 6 July 2026, and the proprietary line is compounding at better than 40%.

**Secular threat: MATERIAL, not terminal.** The relevant structural force is reimbursement compression — government price-setting on high-spend medicines. Daratumumab is exactly the kind of large, long-marketed oncology product that such programmes target, and a negotiated price cut would shrink the royalty base *before* the patents expire, pulling the cliff forward by years. That is material because it hits the single line that funds everything. It is not terminal, because the threat is to one product on a known clock, not to the company's ability to make and sell new antibodies — and the new antibodies are landing. This is also a sector-wide factor shared with every large biopharma name, so it is not a Genmab-specific edge or penalty; it is beta.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.

bull_thesis: The bull case is that the market is paying a fair price for a royalty stream and getting three potential blockbusters for well under what they are worth. Genmab's revenue grew 19% in 2025 and 25% in the first half of 2026 to $2.05 billion, and the full-year outlook was raised on 6 August 2026 to $4.3-4.5 billion. The screen's reported 82% revenue collapse is a reporting-currency artefact (kroner in 2024, US dollars in 2025) and should be ignored. The daratumumab royalty is still growing: Darzalex did $4.21 billion of sales in the second quarter of 2026, so Genmab collects roughly $3.2 billion a year of nearly costless royalty income that funds the pipeline and debt service. Management's delivery record is excellent: the EPCORE FL-1 Phase 3 cut the risk of progression or death by 79% (hazard ratio 0.21, August 2025), the US approval arrived on the 30 November 2025 target date, the European approval followed on 6 July 2026, EPCORE DLBCL-4 met its primary goal on 29 June 2026, and enrolment has repeatedly finished early. Three readouts now guided to the fourth quarter of 2026 could each add billions: frontline EPKINLY plus R-CHOP addresses about 70,000 patients and should be the first frontline bispecific study to report, with subcutaneous dosing suited to community oncology; Rina-S has shown a 50-56% response rate in heavily pretreated ovarian and endometrial cancer with no eye or lung toxicity, and could be first-in-class among next-generation folate-receptor drugs; petosemtamab showed a 63% response rate against 19% for standard care in first-line head and neck cancer. If two of three land, the pipeline alone is worth more than the market implies, the $8.87 billion of acquired intangibles is validated, and leverage falls below 3x by the end of 2027 as promised. Conditions: at least two positive readouts, Darzalex holding its trajectory through 2028, and no disorderly Medicare price negotiation on daratumumab.
bear_thesis: The bear case is that investors are paying a growth multiple for a wasting asset plus a leveraged bet. Roughly 70% of revenue is royalties on other companies' drugs, and the largest, daratumumab, runs on a patent clock that begins to expire around the end of the decade; valued as a declining annuity rather than a perpetuity it is worth about $14 billion, not the $25 billion-plus a flat multiple implies. The balance sheet has changed character: net cash of $1.6 billion at 30 September 2025 became net debt of $3.77 billion at 30 June 2026, with intangibles of $8.87 billion against equity of $5.96 billion, so tangible book is negative and there is no asset floor. About $1.4 billion of the debt floats at a spread over short rates in a market where the Federal Reserve has been hiking and the 10-year Treasury sits near 5%; the weighted cost is about 6.6%. Reported operating profit was flat in the first half of 2026 ($555 million against $548 million) and management warned on 22 September 2026 that spending and amortisation will keep weighing on reported earnings. The pivotal readouts are each binary: the company's claim that Phase 3 results mirror Phase 2 was contradicted by EPCORE DLBCL-1, which missed survival as its sole US primary goal (clarified 23 July 2026), and the fourth-quarter petosemtamab look is an interim response-rate read that will not settle survival. Management refuses to guide peak sales for petosemtamab, the asset it paid about $8 billion for. At 2,318 kroner the shares trade near their 52-week high (2,340), about 29 times 2026 consensus earnings and 20 times 2027, so a single failed readout could take the stock toward 1,900-2,000 kroner, and two failures toward our adverse value near 1,450. What would confirm it: a weak frontline petosemtamab response rate, a frontline DLBCL-2 hazard ratio no better than existing combinations, or a daratumumab price-negotiation selection.
consensus_delta: The street is not pricing terminal decline; if anything, our own screen is. The deep-value signal is an artefact of Genmab switching its reporting currency, and the stock sits at a new 52-week high because the market has the operating facts right: 25% first-half growth and a raised outlook. Where we disagree with the market is narrower and runs in both directions. We are more cautious on the royalty: across five earnings calls, no analyst asked what happens to the daratumumab royalty at loss of exclusivity, and consensus earnings per share that are roughly flat from 2027 to 2029 show the street assumes the new drugs simply replace it. We value it as a declining annuity, which caps the base case. We are more constructive on petosemtamab: the street has no number on it because management refuses to guide one, while we carry it at $5.5 billion, and a clean frontline readout would lift our value by roughly 370 kroner per share. Net, our 2,800 kroner fair value sits modestly above the analyst consensus target (about $38 per depositary receipt, roughly 2,490 kroner, as of our 22 September review), and the gap is almost entirely petosemtamab.
forcing_function: Three readouts, all now guided to the fourth quarter of 2026 (confirmed by management on 22 September 2026). Three pivotal readouts that answer the second question are now guided to the fourth quarter of 2026.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story moved from "royalty company becoming a drug company" to "drug company with a royalty cushion."

- **May 2025 (Q1 2025):** the emphasis is on independence - "becoming a fully integrated biotech independently developing and commercializing wholly owned" medicines, a $3 billion-plus cash pile, and a share buyback of up to 2.2 million shares. Three late-stage bets are named: epcoritamab (sold as EPKINLY), Rina-S and acasunlimab.
- **August 2025 (Q2 2025):** peak confidence. The EPCORE FL-1 Phase 3 trial (a large, randomised trial of the kind regulators approve on) met both goals, cutting the risk of progression or death by 79%. Peak-sales targets appear: over $3 billion for EPKINLY and over $2 billion for Rina-S.

Copenhagen share at 2,377 Danish kroner (DKK), up 5.3% on the day and a new 52-week high (intraday 2,405); the US depositary receipt (ten receipts per share) trades at $35.94, which implies about 6.6 kroner to the dollar. Continuing coverage of our 29 September 2026 look. Evidence base: five earnings calls (8 May 2025, 7 August 2025, 8 November 2025, 17 February 2026, 14 May 2026), the screener's financial block, the first-half 2026 report (6 August 2026), and company announcements through 3 October 2026.*

**Bottom line first.** Genmab is a well-run antibody company whose reported numbers are badly distorted in our own screen. Revenue did not fall 82%: the company switched its reporting currency from kroner to US dollars with the 2025 accounts, and 21.53 billion kroner (2024) against $3.86 billion (2025) produces exactly the printed minus 82.1%. In reality revenue grew 19% in 2025 and 25% in the first quarter of 2026. Management's delivery record is the strongest thing in the file. What is new since our last look is one piece of evidence: on 3 October 2026 Genmab presented the larger Phase 2 data set for Rina-S in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (cancer that has returned within six months of platinum chemotherapy) - a confirmed response rate of 45.9% across 109 patients, with responses lasting a median 12.1 months. That modestly de-risks one of three pipeline pillars. The two big open questions are unchanged: what happens to the daratumumab royalty (Genmab's share of Johnson & Johnson's Darzalex sales, its largest income line) when exclusivity lapses around the end of the decade, and whether the roughly $8 billion Merus purchase, funded with $5.5 billion of new debt, pays off.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story moved from "royalty company becoming a drug company" to "drug company with a royalty cushion, levered to three pivotal readouts."

- **May 2025 (Q1 2025):** independence is the theme - "becoming a fully integrated biotech independently developing and commercializing wholly owned" medicines, over $3 billion of cash, a buyback of up to 2.2 million shares, and Rina-S described as potentially "best-in-class" on a 55.6% response rate in a small ovarian cohort.
- **August 2025 (H1 2025):** the EPCORE FL-1 Phase 3 (EPKINLY plus lenalidomide and rituximab in relapsed follicular lymphoma) cut the risk of progression or death by 79%; Rina-S expands to three Phase 3 trials.
- **November 2025 (Q3 2025):** the Merus acquisition (petosemtamab, a bispecific antibody for head and neck cancer) changes the balance sheet from net cash to net debt.
- **February 2026 (FY 2025):** "2026 will be a defining year" with "up to 6 potentially registrational data readouts." The first stumble is disclosed - EPCORE DLBCL-1 (EPKINLY alone in relapsed large B-cell lymphoma) improved progression-free survival but "overall survival did not reach statistical significance."
- **May 2026 (Q1 2026):** the Rina-S Phase 3 in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer "completed enrollment" early, pulling the pivotal readout into 2026; petosemtamab's trial was upsized.
- **Since (dated, outside the transcripts):** guidance narrowed all three pivotal readouts to the fourth quarter of 2026 (22 September); a 5.11% holder, Darwin Global Management, disclosed on 2 October; the 109-patient Rina-S Phase 2 data were presented on 3 October.

What was quietly de-emphasised: acasunlimab (dropped from the "three pillars" after Merus), and the buyback (not repeated after June 2025, as cash went to Merus).

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Total revenue grew by 19%" (2025) | Screen shows minus 82.1% - but that is kroner-to-dollar translation; $3.86 billion in 2025 vs about $3.2 billion in 2024 equivalent is consistent with +19% | Matches once the currency switch is corrected |
| Proprietary sales "$632 million... up 54%" (2025); Q1 2026 $176 million, +43% | Consistent with revenue growth; still only about 16% of revenue | Matches; royalty dependence remains about 70%+ |
| "Grown operating profit" each year | 2025 net income $999 million, net margin 25.9%; TTM EPS $12.70 vs 2025 $15.94, latest-quarter EPS down 9% year on year | Diverging - reported profit is now falling with Merus amortisation, interest and development spend |
| "Strength of our financial foundation" | Net cash about $3 billion mid-2025 became net debt $3.77 billion at 30 June 2026 (borrowings $5.13 billion + $138 million leases − $1.50 billion cash); debt cost about 6.6% | The foundation is now leveraged; gross leverage target below 3x by end-2027 |
| Free cash flow quality | FCF margin 30.9%, TTM FCF $870 million; Altman-Z 14.8; Piotroski 6/9 | Cash generation real but down sharply from the 2024 level |
| Returns | ROE 17.1%, ROIC 12.6%, gross margin 91.7% "contracting" | Still good, falling as acquired intangibles enter the base |
| Rina-S "best-in-class" | 55.6% response (small cohort, 2025) → 45.9% in 109 patients, median response 12.1 months, activity regardless of folate-receptor level (3 Oct 2026) | Response rate came down with a larger sample, as expected; durability and breadth hold up |

The screen's "deep value" signal (DCF fair value 8,240, owner-earnings +69%) rests on the distorted currency series and on peak royalty earnings capitalised as perpetual. We do not rely on it.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable, confident, increasingly event-focused.** Each call opens with "commitments... delivered." Specificity rose on timing (readouts narrowed to Q4 2026) but stayed low on value: on petosemtamab peak sales the CFO said in February 2026 "I'm not going to front run this" and remained with "multibillion blockbuster potential." On the frontline lymphoma readout the medical chief declined to speculate on a hazard ratio (May 2026). The language shifted from offensive (buybacks, cash pile, 2025) to a disciplined-but-defensive capital stance ("disciplined on OpEx," leverage target) after the debt raise.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

High. Enrolment repeatedly finished ahead of plan (follicular, frontline DLBCL, Rina-S ovarian Phase 3); the follicular US approval landed on its 30 November 2025 target date; revenue guidance was met or raised. The one miss is substantive: the claim that Phase 3 "tended to mimic close Phase II data" was contradicted by EPCORE DLBCL-1, which missed overall survival. The 71% earnings-beat rate (5 of 7 quarters) corroborates a mild conservative bias. Reliability: High, with the caveat that clinical outcomes are not management's to deliver.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Petosemtamab value** - repeatedly asked to quantify; repeatedly declined.
- **Hazard ratio and survival bar for frontline DLBCL** - deflected ("doesn't make much sense to speculate").
- **Readout sequencing** - "I will not comment on which one first or second."
- **The question nobody asks:** across five calls, no analyst asked about the daratumumab royalty after loss of exclusivity, nor the possibility of US Medicare price negotiation on Darzalex. That is the largest single value driver and the street treats it as permanent.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- 🔴 Balance sheet turned from net cash to $3.77 billion net debt (Q4 2025 → Q2 2026); intangibles exceed equity, so tangible book is negative.
- 🔴 EPCORE DLBCL-1 missed survival (January 2026) - weakens the "Phase 3 mirrors Phase 2" claim.
- 🔴 Reported EPS falling (TTM $12.70 vs $15.94 for 2025; latest quarter −9%).
- 🔴 About 70% of revenue is royalty income on other companies' patent-dated drugs.
- 🟢 Revenue +19% (2025), +25% (Q1 2026); proprietary sales +43-54%.
- 🟢 Execution on timelines and approvals; EPKINLY label broadened (hospitalisation recommendation removed, March 2026).
- 🟢 Rina-S 109-patient Phase 2: 45.9% response, 12.1-month median duration, 51% of responders still responding at one year (3 October 2026).
- 🟢 A new 5.11% institutional holder (Darwin, 2 October 2026) - informational, not a catalyst.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- "Antibody company" has become "late-stage portfolio" language; the platform (DuoBody, HexaBody) is now described mainly as the source of future internal assets.
- Capital allocation vocabulary changed from "buyback" (2025) to "gross leverage below 3x" (2026) - the buyback is gone for now.
- The CFO's refusal to put a number on petosemtamab, the most expensive asset the company has ever bought, is the most telling non-answer in the file.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**PIVOTING.** Genmab has converted a royalty cash machine into a leveraged bet on three internally owned late-stage drugs. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: the base case leans on a royalty with a patent clock (more than half of value), while the upside leans on one binary readout (frontline petosemtamab) that underwrites an $8 billion purchase financed with debt.

**Moat:** intangible (patents plus antibody-engineering know-how and royalty contracts). Narrow but real: 91.7% gross margin and 12.6% ROIC are good, and the decline in returns reflects acquisition accounting and leverage rather than competitive erosion; trend broadly stable. **Secular threat:** manageable - US drug-price negotiation (reimbursement compression) and ordinary patent expiry, not a structural shrinking of the business. The screen's cheapness is a data artefact, not a fear-print or a value trap; at 2,377 kroner the shares are fairly to fully priced on our numbers.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

bull_thesis: The bull case is that the market is paying a fair price for a royalty stream and getting two de-risked growth franchises plus a third potential blockbuster for less than they are worth. Revenue grew 19% in 2025 and 25% in the first half of 2026; the screen's 82% revenue collapse is a reporting-currency artefact (kroner in 2024, US dollars in 2025). The daratumumab royalty (Genmab's share of Johnson & Johnson's Darzalex sales; Darzalex sold $4.2 billion worldwide in the second quarter of 2026) is still growing and throws off roughly $3 billion a year of nearly costless income that funds the pipeline and services the debt. Management delivers: EPCORE FL-1 cut the risk of progression or death by 79%, EPCORE DLBCL-4 was positive in June 2026, and on 5 October 2026 EPCORE DLBCL-2 cut that risk by 51% in newly diagnosed large B-cell lymphoma (hazard ratio 0.49 at the first interim), the largest market EPKINLY can reach and a result that compares favourably with the roughly 27% risk reduction that set Roche's Polivy as the frontline standard. EPKINLY already grew 48% to $312 million in the first half of 2026 before this label. bear_thesis: The bear case is that investors are paying a full price for a wasting royalty plus a leveraged bet. consensus_delta: The street is not pricing terminal decline; our own screen mispriced it the other way, because the deep-value signal is a reporting-currency artefact. Where we disagree with the market is narrower and runs both ways. We are more cautious on the royalty: across five earnings calls no analyst asked what happens to the daratumumab royalty at loss of exclusivity, and roughly flat consensus earnings from 2027 to 2029 show the street assumes new drugs simply replace it; we value it as a declining annuity, which caps the base case. forcing_function: Two readouts remain guided to the fourth quarter of 2026. valley_of_death: Nothing forces a sale before value converges. There is no debt maturity wall in the next nine months; the $5.5 billion was raised in late 2025, and management targets gross leverage below 3x by end-2027. # Genmab A/S (GMAB.CO) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*As of 26 October 2026. Copenhagen share at 2,964 Danish kroner (DKK) on the licensed live quote (FMP, 26 October 2026, up about 12% on the day from a 2,644 previous close; day range 2,915-3,060, a new 52-week high), the dollar at 6.685 kroner (FMP spot, 26 October 2026). Continuing coverage of our 19 October 2026 look. Evidence base: five earnings calls (7 August 2025, 8 November 2025, 17 February 2026, 14 May 2026, 6 August 2026), the screener's financial block, the first-half 2026 report (6 August 2026), and company announcements through 26 October 2026.*

**What changed since 19 October 2026.** A lot, and all of it on the good side. On 23 October 2026 Genmab reported that the Phase 3 RAINFOL-02 trial of Rina-S (rinatabart sesutecan, an antibody-drug conjugate - an antibody that carries a chemotherapy payload to the tumour - aimed at folate receptor alpha) in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer met its primary endpoint, progression-free survival, and its key secondary endpoint, overall survival, against investigator's-choice chemotherapy, regardless of folate-receptor level or prior mirvetuximab (AbbVie's Elahere). An overall-survival win in this setting is the strongest result the trial could have produced; the hazard ratios were not disclosed and will be presented at a future medical meeting. On 25 and 26 October 2026, at the European Society for Medical Oncology congress, Genmab updated petosemtamab Phase 2 data: in first-line PD-L1-positive head and neck cancer with pembrolizumab, median overall survival of 28.2 months, a 63% response rate, 9.0 months median progression-free survival and 19% complete responses (43 evaluable patients); in colorectal cancer, response rates of 75% first-line and 67% second-line (81% in left-sided first-line tumours) at short follow-up. On 24 October 2026 Genmab and Incyte agreed a clinical collaboration combining petosemtamab with Incyte's KRAS G12D inhibitor in first-line colorectal cancer (no economics disclosed; immaterial to value today). The frontline petosemtamab Phase 3 topline is still "anticipated later this year." The shares have risen from about 2,445 kroner at our last look to 2,964, about 21%.

**Bottom line first.** Genmab is a well-run antibody company whose reported numbers are badly distorted in our own screen, and whose management has now delivered three positive pivotal readouts in five months (EPCORE DLBCL-4 in June, EPCORE DLBCL-2 on 5 October, RAINFOL-02 on 23 October 2026). Revenue did not fall 82%: the company switched its reporting currency from kroner to US dollars with the 2025 accounts; in reality revenue grew 19% in 2025 and 25% in the first half of 2026. Of the three fourth-quarter binaries we flagged last week, two have now resolved positively. One open question remains on the pipeline side - the frontline petosemtamab Phase 3, which tests the roughly $8 billion Merus purchase - and the structural question is unchanged: what happens to the daratumumab royalty (Genmab's share of Johnson & Johnson's Darzalex sales, its largest income line) when exclusivity lapses around the end of the decade. The business case is stronger than a week ago; the price has moved faster than our value.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story moved from "royalty company becoming a drug company" to "drug company with a royalty cushion, levered to pivotal readouts" - and in the second half of 2026 those readouts landed one after another.

- **August 2025 (H1 2025):** EPCORE FL-1 cut the risk of progression or death by 79% in relapsed follicular lymphoma; Rina-S expands to three Phase 3 trials.
- **November 2025 (Q3 2025):** the Merus acquisition (petosemtamab) changes the balance sheet from net cash to net debt.
- **February 2026 (FY 2025):** "2026 will be a defining year." First stumble: EPCORE DLBCL-1 improved progression-free survival but missed on overall survival.
- **May 2026 (Q1 2026):** the Rina-S Phase 3 completed enrollment early, pulling the readout into 2026.
- **August 2026 (H1 2026):** revenue "grew by 25%"; EPCORE DLBCL-4 positive (June); EPKINLY first-half sales $312 million, up 48%; "3 super important phase 3 studies reading out in the coming months."
- **October 2026 (dated, outside the transcripts):** 3 October, Rina-S 109-patient Phase 2 (45.9% confirmed response); 5 October, EPCORE DLBCL-2 positive (hazard ratio 0.49); 23 October, RAINFOL-02 Phase 3 positive on progression-free and overall survival; 25-26 October, petosemtamab Phase 2 updates (28.2-month median overall survival first-line head and neck); 24 October, Incyte collaboration.

What was quietly de-emphasised: acasunlimab, immunology ("cancer is clearly the priority for us right now," August 2026) and the buyback.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "We grew total revenue by 25%" (H1 2026) | Screen shows minus 82.1% for 2025 - a kroner-to-dollar translation artefact; underlying 2025 growth +19% | Matches once the currency switch is corrected |
| EPKINLY "$312 million... a 48% increase" (H1 2026) | Proprietary sales rising fast, still roughly a fifth of revenue | Matches; royalty dependence still about 70% |
| "Growing operating profits" | Trailing EPS $12.70 vs $15.94 for 2025; latest-quarter EPS down 9% | Diverging - amortisation, interest and development spend weigh |
| Financial strength | Net debt $3.77 billion at 30 June 2026 (borrowings $5.13 billion + $138 million leases - $1.50 billion cash) | Leveraged; gross leverage target below 3x by end-2027 |
| Cash generation | FCF margin 30.9%, trailing FCF $870 million; Altman-Z 16.6; Piotroski 6/9 | Real, below the 2024 level |
| Rina-S Phase 3 to read out in 2026 and support a 2027 launch (May and August 2026) | 23 October 2026: RAINFOL-02 met progression-free and overall survival | Delivered, on time, with the stronger endpoint |
| Petosemtamab "multibillion" (August 2026) | 26 October 2026: 28.2-month median overall survival in 43 first-line patients (Phase 2) | Supportive; the Phase 3 is the real test |

The screen's "deep value" signal (DCF fair value 8,277, owner-earnings +64%) rests on the distorted currency series and capitalises peak royalty earnings as perpetual. We do not rely on it.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rising, confident, now vindicated.** In August 2026 the chief executive said "we are in a really good place"; two of the three pivotal readouts he pointed to have since come in positive. Specificity on value stays low: petosemtamab peak sales remain "multibillion" with no number; topline releases give primary endpoints, with detail later (the RAINFOL-02 release gave no hazard ratios).

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

High. Enrolment repeatedly finished ahead of plan; the follicular approval landed on its target date; revenue guidance was raised in August 2026; DLBCL-2 and RAINFOL-02 both reported in the guided quarter and both were positive. The one substantive miss remains EPCORE DLBCL-1's overall-survival failure (January 2026). Earnings beat in 5 of 7 quarters. Reliability: High, with the caveat that clinical outcomes are not management's to deliver.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Petosemtamab value and data format** - asked to quantify, declined; topline will be primary endpoint only.
- **EPKINLY patent life** - management would only say "mid thirties."
- **Competition for Rina-S** - the medical chief acknowledged "multiple folate receptor ADCs from very large competitors." The RAINFOL-02 win regardless of receptor level and after mirvetuximab answers part of this, but commercial share against AbbVie is still ahead.
- **The question nobody asks:** across five calls, no analyst asked about the daratumumab royalty after loss of exclusivity, nor US Medicare price negotiation on Darzalex.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: balance sheet net debt of $3.77 billion (30 June 2026); intangibles exceed equity, tangible book negative.
- Red: reported EPS falling (trailing $12.70 vs $15.94 for 2025).
- Red: about 70% of revenue is royalty income on other companies' patent-dated drugs.
- Red: RAINFOL-02 and DLBCL-2 magnitudes not yet fully disclosed (no hazard ratios for RAINFOL-02; no overall survival for DLBCL-2).
- Red: the shares are up about 21% in a week and sit at a 52-week high, about 54% above the 200-day average - event-anticipation holders now own a lot of it.
- Green: RAINFOL-02 positive on progression-free and overall survival (23 October 2026).
- Green: EPCORE DLBCL-2 positive at the first interim, hazard ratio 0.49 (5 October 2026).
- Green: petosemtamab first-line head and neck median overall survival 28.2 months in Phase 2 (26 October 2026), roughly double what pembrolizumab alone has historically achieved in this setting (cross-trial, indicative only).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- "Antibody company" language has become "late-stage portfolio" language.
- Capital-allocation vocabulary changed from "buyback" (2025) to "gross leverage below 3x" (2026).
- Releasing updated Phase 2 overall survival on petosemtamab weeks before its Phase 3 topline is a confidence signal, but also a way to frame expectations ahead of a primary-endpoint-only topline.
- The refusal to put a number on petosemtamab remains the most telling non-answer in the file.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**PIVOTING, and the pivot is working.** Genmab converted a royalty cash machine into a leveraged bet on three internally owned late-stage drugs; two of the three (EPKINLY frontline, Rina-S) have now delivered pivotal wins. The single thing to weigh before sizing: the price has run ahead of the value - at 2,964 kroner the discount to our raised fair value is well below what this book needs - and more than 40% of value is still a royalty on a patent clock, while the frontline petosemtamab Phase 3 (guided to later in 2026) still underwrites the debt-funded Merus purchase.

**Moat:** intangible (patents, antibody-engineering know-how, royalty contracts). Narrow but real: 91.7% gross margin and 12.6% ROIC; the fall in returns reflects acquisition accounting and leverage, not competitive erosion; the proprietary franchise is widening. **Secular threat:** manageable - US drug-price negotiation and ordinary patent expiry.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

As of 2026-11-10. Price used: 3,581 DKK (Copenhagen listing, FMP quote 2026-11-10, down 2.2% on the day). Transcripts covered: Q3 2025 (2025-11-08), full-year 2025 (2026-02-17), Q1 2026 (2026-05-14), first half 2026 (2026-08-06) and Q3 2026 (2026-11-05).

- **Full-year 2025 (2026-02-17):** guidance year; leverage commitment introduced ("below 3x gross leverage by the end of 2027").
- **Q1 2026 (2026-05-14):** revenue +25%; RAINFOL-02 (Rina-S, platinum-resistant ovarian cancer) completed enrollment early, pulling the readout into 2026. Management called 2026 "a very catalyst-rich year".
